history: Antares B swims inside the blood-red glow of one of the largest stars known — a hot blue-white B2.5 dwarf orbiting some 550 AU out, deep inside the supergiant's swollen envelope of ejected gas. Observers since the 19th century have called it green: an optical illusion born of the extreme color and brightness contrast, a little white spark lost beside a swollen red sun ~680 times the diameter of ours. The pair spans more than five magnitudes of difference — the companion only emerges in steady, very good seeing, a test observers have chased since the founding of modern astronomy.
